decisions: Interpret '?' and blank/null-like tokens as missing, rather than as categories or zero.
Strip surrounding whitespace and normalize category case before checking duplicates.
Correct make labels alfa-romero -> alfa-romeo and peugot -> peugeot; preserve the raw source.
Parse 18 numerical columns, including word-encoded door/cylinder counts; symboling remains ordinal.
Set nonnumeric, nonfinite, or impossible values to missing and record their counts.
Remove only exact duplicates across all 26 normalized fields; retain differing variants.
Keep missing numerical values, without imputation; use complete observations for each question.
Keep plausible IQR outliers: an unusual luxury or performance car is not automatically a data error.

charts.title: Price distribution
charts.observation: The mean price is 13,207, compared with a median of 10,295; sample skewness is 1.81. The higher mean and long upper tail indicate right skew.

charts.title: Most represented makes
charts.observation: Toyota contributes 32 of 205 records (15.6%). The dataset contains 22 makes; these counts describe dataset composition, not market share.

charts.title: Fuel-type representation
charts.observation: gas: 185 records (90.2%); diesel: 20 records (9.8%). The imbalance limits comparisons between fuel groups.

charts.title: Price by body style
charts.observation: Hardtop cars have the highest group median (19,688; n=8). Group sizes differ; the boxes show spread, and isolated points are IQR flags rather than proven errors.

charts.title: Engine size, price, and fuel type
charts.observation: Engine size and price have Pearson r=0.872 across 201 complete pairs. Fuel colour adds a third variable; the pooled association does not isolate an engine-size effect or establish causation.

charts.title: Horsepower and fuel economy
charts.observation: Horsepower and highway MPG have Pearson r=-0.771 (n=203). Higher-power cars tend to have lower fuel economy in this sample; MPG measures efficiency, not distance driven.

charts.title: Numerical feature relationships
charts.observation: City and highway MPG are closely related (r=0.971). Cell sample sizes range from 199 to 205 because missing values are excluded pair by pair. Correlations involving similar measurements can be redundant.

charts.title: Mean prices by make
charts.observation: Among makes with at least five priced records, mercedes-benz has the highest mean price (33,647; n=8). Only the top eight eligible makes are shown; the minimum count reduces very small-group comparisons but does not remove sampling bias.

findings: Prices are right-skewed: mean 13,207, median 10,295, skewness 1.81 across 201 known prices.
Toyota is the most represented make: 32/205 records (15.6%). This is sample composition, not market share.
The fuel mix is imbalanced: gas 185, diesel 20.
Larger engines are associated with higher prices: Pearson r=0.872 using 201 complete pairs.
Horsepower is negatively associated with highway MPG: Pearson r=-0.771 using 203 complete pairs.
mercedes-benz has the highest mean price among makes with at least five known prices: 33,647 (n=8).
The price IQR rule flags 14/201 records outside [-5,312, 29,588]. These observations are retained.
